title: Shoulder joint anatomy
description: Mobility bought at the price of stability: a shallow glenoid, a loose capsule, and four rotator-cuff tendons doing the holding.

questions.question: Why can the shoulder move so freely?
questions.answer: The shallow glenoid cavity permits a wide range of movement. The labrum, capsule, rotator cuff and surrounding muscles help stabilize the humeral head.

questions.question: Which muscles form the rotator cuff?
questions.answer: Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis form the rotator cuff around the glenohumeral joint.

questions.question: What is the supraspinatus tendon?
questions.answer: Over the top of the humeral head. Function: Initiates abduction (first 15°).

questions.question: Where is the teres minor tendon located?
questions.answer: Below infraspinatus. Function: External rotation + capsule tension.

questions.question: What is the function of the glenoid labrum?
questions.answer: Function: Adds ~50% of glenoid depth. Fibrocartilage rim deepening the socket.
